english_explanations: To settle down to rest, as a bird on a branch; the place where birds rest.

chinese_translations.example: Crows return to their roost at dusk.
Crows return to their roost at dusk.

english_explanations: To sit on eggs to keep them warm until they hatch.

chinese_translations.example: The female incubates the eggs while the male brings food.
The female incubates the eggs while the male brings food.

english_explanations: A hole or tunnel dug by an animal to live in; to dig such a hole.

chinese_translations.example: Earthworms burrow deep into the soil.
Rabbits burrowed beneath the hedgerow.

english_explanations: The resting place of a wild animal, especially a fierce one.

chinese_translations.example: The wolves returned to their lair with the kill.

english_explanations: The hidden home of a wild animal, such as a cave or hollow.

chinese_translations.example: a bear's/lion's den

english_explanations: To search widely for food or supplies.

chinese_translations.example: Capuchins forage for fruit in the canopy.

english_explanations: To feed on dead animals that one has not killed oneself.

chinese_translations.example: Hyenas both hunt and scavenge.
Hyenas both hunt and scavenge.

english_explanations: The act of one animal killing and eating another.

chinese_translations.example: Nest predation by stoats devastated the colony.
Nest predation by stoats devastated the colony.

english_explanations: A close, long-term interaction between two different species living together.

chinese_translations.example: The ants and their fungus live in symbiosis.
The ants and their fungus live in symbiosis.

english_explanations: Mating among closely related individuals, which reduces genetic diversity.

chinese_translations.example: Small isolated populations suffer from inbreeding.

english_explanations: Tiny drifting animals in water that feed on phytoplankton.

chinese_translations.example: Zooplankton swarm in the sunlit surface waters.

english_explanations: Microscopic drifting algae that photosynthesize in water.

chinese_translations.example: Phytoplankton produce much of the ocean's oxygen.

english_explanations: A species able to thrive on a wide range of foods and habitats.

chinese_translations.example: Rats are generalists that survive in almost any habitat.
Rats are generalists that survive in almost any habitat.

english_explanations: (of animals) travelling from one region to another with the seasons.

chinese_translations.example: migratory flights/birds
Migratory birds cross the Sahara each autumn.

english_explanations: To pass the winter, often dormant or in a milder place; the act of doing so.

chinese_translations.example: The butterflies overwinter in the mountains of Mexico.

english_explanations: To clean and smooth fur or feathers, alone or mutually.

chinese_translations.example: Otters groom their fur constantly to keep it waterproof.
Otters groom their fur constantly to keep it waterproof.

english_explanations: To twist the body about, as when uncomfortable or trying to escape.

chinese_translations.example: The crayfish squirmed in the otter's paws.
The children were squirming restlessly in their seats.

english_explanations: (of a bird) to sing with a continuous alternating flow of notes.

chinese_translations.example: The bird warbled a bubbling song at first light.
The bird warbled a bubbling song at first light.

english_explanations: To make a sudden forward movement or attack.

chinese_translations.example: The barracuda lunged at the flashing lure.
The barracuda lunged at the flashing lure.

english_explanations: To eat up eagerly and completely.

chinese_translations.example: The chicks devour whatever the parents bring.
The chicks devour whatever the parents bring.

english_explanations: To take food or other substances into the body.

chinese_translations.example: Caterpillars ingest toxins from the leaves they eat.
Caterpillars ingest toxins from the leaves they eat.

english_explanations: To force something out of the body or a container.

chinese_translations.example: to expel air from the lungs
The termites expel stale air through chimneys in the mound.

english_explanations: A wavelike motion, as of a fish's body when swimming.

chinese_translations.example: Eels swim by undulation of the whole body.
Eels swim by undulation of the whole body.

english_explanations: The force that drives a body forward; relating to such force.

chinese_translations.example: wind/steam/jet propulsion
Otters gain propulsion from their muscular tails.

english_explanations: The ability of a body to float in a fluid.

chinese_translations.example: The boat bobbed like a cork on the waves: light and buoyant.

english_explanations: Shaped to reduce resistance when moving through air or water.

chinese_translations.example: Tuna have streamlined bodies built for speed.
The cars all have a new streamlined design.

english_explanations: The ability to change direction quickly and easily.

chinese_translations.example: Broad pectoral fins give the fish great maneuverability.
Broad pectoral fins give the fish great maneuverability.

english_explanations: To make surfaces smooth and slippery so they move easily.

chinese_translations.example: Mucus lubricates the fish's body as it swims.

english_explanations: Thick and sticky; not flowing freely.

chinese_translations.example: Seawater feels more viscous than air to a swimming fish.

english_explanations: A fluid's resistance to flow; its thickness.

chinese_translations.example: Cool water rises in viscosity and slows the swimmer.
Cool water rises in viscosity and slows the swimmer.

english_explanations: To pass beyond an intended point or limit.

chinese_translations.example: Some migrants overshoot their breeding grounds in strong winds.
Some migrants overshoot their breeding grounds in strong winds.

english_explanations: To fly over or across a place.

chinese_translations.example: We overflew the war zone, taking photographs.
